resources.string: VoxCtrl voice keyboard is not turned on yet. Turn it on in the system\'s keyboard list, then choose it.
The keyboard is turned on. Choose it to start dictating.
VoxCtrl voice keyboard is your current keyboard.
Microphone access is allowed. The microphone is on only between your tap to start and your tap to stop.
The keyboard needs the microphone to record a dictation.
Microphone access was refused. Allow it under Permissions in this app\'s system settings.

Dictation is transcribed by your own VoxCtrl server. On the server, run voxctrl-server --pairing-code and paste the code here. To reach the server over Tailscale, enter its tailnet name or 100.x address first: an address you enter is kept, and the code fills in the rest.
This server is version %1$s. The keyboard needs %2$s or newer.
This server (VoxCtrl %1$s) talks to apps in a newer way than this keyboard understands. Update VoxCtrl Keys.
Paired. The address and key are filled in.
Pairing removed. The saved certificate is forgotten.
Tailscale address: the tailnet encrypts this connection.
Local network address: audio is not encrypted on the way to the server. Fine on a network you trust. Turn on encryption on the server to protect it.
Warning: this address is on the internet and the connection is not encrypted. Your audio and API key would be readable in transit. Use Tailscale, or turn on encryption on the server and pair again.
HTTPS address: the connection is encrypted.
Sends what you have said so far to your server a few times a second. Turn it off for a slow server.
Leave empty for the server\'s setting (e.g. en)
Words to listen for, separated by commas
On a wide screen, such as an unfolded phone, the typing keyboard is narrower than the screen and sits under one thumb. Tap the keyboard button on the left of the bar to show or hide it.
Tap here, switch to the VoxCtrl keyboard and speak

This keyboard talks only to the server you enter above. It has no analytics, no crash reporting and no account. Audio is held in memory while you dictate and is never written to storage; text is typed into the app you are using and not kept. The API key is encrypted on this device and left out of backups.
